scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
This is an executive summary. What customer source material do I have to work with (RFP text, discovery notes, the CFO's own stated words)? I'll treat the prompt's details as the supplied facts — the CFO's own stated priorities ($1,850,000 annual spend, DOT compliance audit in 6 months) and the programme figures given (28 SQL Server instances, 620 Hyper-V VMs, $4,200,000 over 2 years, targeting GCE and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL). No other source material (discovery notes, RFP text) was supplied, so `PF-3.3` cannot fire — every term is judged by the deletion test alone. Drafting now.

**Executive summary**

---

Rachel, you are measured on two things this year: bringing technology spend down from its current $1,850,000 run rate, and walking into a clean Department of Transportation compliance audit that opens in six months. Today, your load-matching and carrier-settlement systems run on 28 on-premises Microsoft SQL Server instances across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines — infrastructure you own, patch, and pay for whether or not it is fully utilized [PF-2.11 GAP: current utilization or idle-capacity figures for the 620 VMs were not supplied]. We propose moving that estate to Google Cloud over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme: Google Compute Engine replaces the Hyper-V layer, and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL replaces the SQL Server instances, so your teams stop maintaining hypervisor and database infrastructure and start consuming it as a managed service [PF-1.17 GAP: a named, checkable comparable — a similarly sized freight brokerage migration this vendor has delivered — was not supplied].

Two things should happen on a predictable schedule. First, your infrastructure cost profile shifts from a fixed $1,850,000 annual spend to a consumption model tied to actual load-matching and settlement volume [PF-2.11 GAP: no projected post-migration run-rate or payback timeline was supplied, so the size and timing of the reduction cannot be stated]. Second, ahead of your audit in six months, the migration gives your compliance team a single, logged, access-controlled data layer in Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in place of 28 separately administered SQL Server instances — fewer systems to reconcile evidence across when the auditor asks for it [PF-2.17 REVIEW (compliance): which DOT audit controls this data-layer consolidation actually satisfies, and whether Google Cloud's own certifications cover your specific compliance scope, needs confirmation before this claim ships]. We will size the cutover sequence and cost timeline against your audit date in the next planning session, so neither commitment lands on you unverified.

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| Current utilization/idle-capacity figures for the 620 Hyper-V VMs | PF-2.11 | Actual or estimated utilization data for the existing VM fleet, to ground the "pay whether or not fully utilized" claim |
| Named, checkable migration comparable | PF-1.17 | A reference migration (freight brokerage or similar scale) this vendor can actually produce as proof |
| Post-migration run-rate / payback timeline | PF-2.11 | Projected annual cost after migration and the timeline to realize savings against the $1,850,000 baseline |
| DOT audit controls satisfied by data-layer consolidation | PF-2.17 | Confirmation of which specific DOT audit requirements the Cloud SQL consolidation addresses, and applicable Google Cloud compliance certifications |
